The minimum is **10**, but I could not fully verify this. I ruled out 6 and did not establish that 10 is realizable.

**Ruling out 6.** The only connected cubic graph on 6 vertices that could work is the triangular prism, since K₄ is impossible (no four mutually touching equal circles fit in the plane). In a penny graph, the prism's two triangles must be unit-side triangles with each matched pair joined by the same translation vector v, where |v| = 1. Non-adjacent pairs require |u + v| ≥ 1 for each side vector u, which forces |u·v| ≤ 1/2 for all three side directions. Those three directions differ by 60°, and no direction v satisfies all three conditions at once. So the prism is not a penny graph.

**Why 10.** Checking the smaller cubic graphs (on 8 vertices, e.g. the cube) by hand is not conclusive. I recall the 10-vertex bound from the literature on regular penny graphs, but I did not reconstruct an explicit 10-vertex embedding or confirm the lower bound for 8.

ANSWER: 10
